hints: Sort the coin values from smallest to largest.
Suppose all sums from 1 through x-1 are reachable; a coin no larger than x extends this to x+coin.
The first coin larger than x leaves x itself impossible.
analogy: Build a consecutive covered range of sums, extending its right edge with each usable coin.
example: Coins 1,2,5 cover 1..3, then 5 starts a gap at 4, so 4 is the smallest impossible sum.
algorithm: Sort coins and set x=1. For each coin c, if c>x stop; otherwise set x+=c. Print x.
correctness: By induction the currently reachable sums include every value below x; a coin c<=x extends that interval continuously, while c>x cannot form x.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) extra space beyond sorting.
